cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Clarification from the agency - Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation, and reasonable research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the and law enforcement communities. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.

For GS-11: One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-09 in federal, state, or local government or equivalent public or private sector, performing the following: collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; presenting briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions and recommendations; and producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.

cond_0024.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public. Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. You will work as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility, staying in regular contact with counterparts across the intelligence and law enforcement communities.
cond_0024.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of a Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, you will actively clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, request data to substantiate or verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation, and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. You will regularly connect with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities to perform liaison and coordination functions. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated database systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
You will actively clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, request data to substantiate and verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation, and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. A regular part of the role is performing liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence and law enforcement communities, initiating discussions to resolve issues and keep investigations on track. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations.
cond_0024.requirements:
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. Minimum Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Must sign a mobility agreement as described above.
For GS-11: One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-09 in federal, state, local government, or equivalent public or private sector, actively performing the following:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations.
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents.
Presenting briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations.
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports.
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions, and recommendations.
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
For GS-12: One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-11 in federal, state, local government, or equivalent public or private sector, actively performing the following:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations.
Facilitating investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces.
Serving as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked].
Utilizing seasoned judgment and experience in intelligence operations.
Conducting long-range planning in assigned area of responsibility considering actual and potential problems and presenting findings to supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Note: Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for GS-12.
Preferred Requirements
For GS-11 only, in lieu of specialized experience, candidates may qualify with:
A Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree, or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a related field such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, sociology, or another field that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the position.
LL.M., if related.
A combination of education and experience (calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application).

cond_0028.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Clarification from the agency - Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
cond_0028.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation, and reasonable research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the and law enforcement communities. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.
cond_0028.requirements:
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements:
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. See www.sss.gov
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-9.
GS-11 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-09 grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Presenting briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions and recommendations; and
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience you may qualify for the GS-11 with a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a field of study related to this position such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, and sociology or other field of study that provides them with knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related
OR
Combination of education and experience. This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for the GS-12, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-11.
GS-12 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-11 Grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Facilitates the investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Serves as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Utilizes seasoned judgement and experience in intelligence operations; and
Conducts long-range planning in assigned area of responsibility considering actual and potential problems and presents findings to supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for this grade level GS-12.

cond_0039.intro: We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team.
cond_0039.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation, and reasonable research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the and law enforcement communities. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.

Minimum Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. See www.sss.gov
For GS-11: Around one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in federal, state, or local government, or equivalent public or private sector experience, with working knowledge of the following:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using intelligence-gathering methods such as link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents
Presenting briefings on intelligence topics to law enforcement and intelligence agencies
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports
Drafting complex intelligence reports that contain analyses, conclusions, and recommendations
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources
OR a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree, or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education in a related field such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, sociology, or a field that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of this position — or equivalent practical experience.
OR LL.M., if related.
OR a combination of education and experience, calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
For GS-12: Around one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in federal, state, or local government, or equivalent public or private sector experience, with working knowledge of the following:
Using intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations
Facilitating investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces
Serving as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]
Applying sound judgment and experience in intelligence operations
Conducting long-range planning in an assigned area of responsibility, considering actual and potential problems, and presenting findings to a supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist
Note: Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for GS-12.
Preferred Requirements
Background in interagency coordination or liaison work across intelligence or law enforcement communities
Familiarity with ICTAP or CTAP eligibility processes
Veteran preference eligibility (submit required documentation with application)

cond_0047.intro:
We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team.
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Clarification from the agency - Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
cond_0047.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation, and reasonable research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the and law enforcement communities. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.
cond_0047.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements:
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. See www.sss.gov
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-9.
GS-11 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-09 Grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Demonstrated expertise in collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; with a strong command of a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Proven track record in extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Exceptional ability to present briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Deep knowledge of maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Advanced proficiency in drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions and recommendations; and
Substantial experience producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience you may qualify for the GS-11 with a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree required; or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a field of study related to this position such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, and sociology or other field of study that provides them with knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related
OR
Combination of education and experience. This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for the GS-12, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-11.
GS-12 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-11 Grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Deep expertise in a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Demonstrated expertise facilitating investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Proven track record serving as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Extensive seasoned judgement and experience in intelligence operations; and
Strong command of conducting long-range planning in assigned area of responsibility considering actual and potential problems, with the ability to present findings clearly to supervisors or senior intelligence research specialists.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for this grade level GS-12.
Please do not cut and paste the position description, specialized experience, or occupational assessment questionnaire from this announcement into your resume, as this will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Veteran Preference: If you are entitled to veteran preference, you should indicate the type of veteran preference you are claiming on your résumé.
In order to verify your veteran preference entitlement, please submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214 (Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty); official statement of service from your command if you are currently on active duty; or other official documentation (e.g., documentation of receipt of a campaign badge or expeditionary medal) that shows your military service was performed under honorable conditions.
In addition, if you are a disabled veteran, a Purple Heart recipient, or widow/widower of a veteran, the spouse of a disabled veteran or the natural mother of a disabled or deceased veteran, you must submit the October 2013 Revised Standard Form (SF) 15, ""Application for 10-Point Veteran Preference,"" and the other required documentation identified on the reverse side of the SF-15 to support your preference claim.

cond_0070.intro:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. The role functions as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0070.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of a Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenues of investigation, and researches information for use in responding to collateral requests.
Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, including internal and external automated database systems, intelligence reports, and case files.
Produces detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups.
Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations.
Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts.
Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information.
Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports.
Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel across the intelligence community as required.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenues of investigation, and researches information for use in responding to collateral requests.
Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources.
Produces detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups.
Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel across the intelligence and law enforcement communities as required by operational needs.
Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts.
Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports.
Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations.

May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 grade level in federal, state, or local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Preparing and delivering briefings on intelligence topics to law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions, and recommendations; and
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience, a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree, or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a related field such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, sociology, or another field that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related.
OR
Combination of education and experience, calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for GS-12, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in federal, state, or local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Facilitating investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Serving as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Applying seasoned judgment and experience in intelligence operations; and
Conducting long-range planning in an assigned area of responsibility, considering actual and potential problems, and documenting findings for review by a supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for GS-12.

cond_0141.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. The role involves regular engagement with counterparts across the intelligence and law enforcement communities, and a significant part of the work involves staying in contact with investigators, analysts, and agency personnel to share findings and support ongoing operations. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0141.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, actively clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenues of investigation, and researches information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups and communicates findings clearly to relevant personnel. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information, regularly connecting with requestors to clarify needs and walk them through results. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs ongoing liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities, initiating contact to resolve questions and keep stakeholders informed.

Under the guidance of a Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, help clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, coordinate requests for data to substantiate or verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation, and support research for use in responding to collateral requests. Provide detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups. Share recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and help establish new collection techniques for unique investigations. Work with counterparts to conduct validation of sources and evaluate information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and support production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Coordinate with local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Help develop and maintain computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Perform liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.

Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.

Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.

[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public. Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
Most people become stronger in this kind of analytical and intelligence work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0212.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation, and reasonable research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation and research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the and law enforcement communities. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.
cond_0212.requirements:
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements:
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. See www.sss.gov
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-9.
GS-11 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-09 grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Presenting briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions and recommendations; and
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience you may qualify for the GS-11 with a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a field of study related to this position such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, and sociology or other field of study that provides them with knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related
OR
Combination of education and experience. This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for the GS-12, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-11.
GS-12 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-11 Grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Facilitates the investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Serves as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Utilizes seasoned judgement and experience in intelligence operations; and
Conducts long-range planning in assigned area of responsibility considering actual and potential problems and presents findings to supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for this grade level GS-12.

We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team.
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Clarification from the agency - Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
cond_0216.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to support the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will work as an all-source intelligence analyst, sharing responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of a Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, help clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, coordinate requests for data to substantiate or verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation, and support research for use in responding to collateral requests. Coordinate complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated database systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provide detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups. Share recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and help establish new collection techniques for unique investigations. Work with counterparts to conduct validation of sources and evaluate information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and support production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Coordinate with local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Help develop and maintain computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Perform liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Help clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, coordinate requests for data to substantiate and verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation and support research for use in responding to collateral requests. Coordinate complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Provide detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups. Perform liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel throughout the law enforcement communities. Work with counterparts to conduct validation of sources and evaluate information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and support production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Help develop and maintain computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Share recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and help establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.
cond_0216.requirements:
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements:
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. See www.sss.gov
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-9.
GS-11 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-09 grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Presenting briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions and recommendations; and
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience you may qualify for the GS-11 with a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a field of study related to this position such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, and sociology or other field of study that provides them with knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related
OR
Combination of education and experience. This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for the GS-12, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-11.
GS-12 - You Qualify If You Possess One Year Of Specialized Experience, Equivalent To The GS-11 Grade Level In The Federal, State, Or Local Government Or Equivalent Public Or Private Sector Experience, Performing The Following Duties:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Facilitates the investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Serves as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Utilizes seasoned judgement and experience in intelligence operations; and
Conducts long-range planning in assigned area of responsibility considering actual and potential problems and presents findings to supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for this grade level GS-12.

cond_0228.responsibilities:

The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenue of investigation, and reasonable research information for use in responding to collateral requests. Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated data base systems, intelligence reports and case files. Provides detailed analytical reports of the activities of crime groups. Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations. Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information. Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.

We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team.
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Clarification from the agency - Applications will be accepted from all [Location masked] citizens.
cond_0243.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to support the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will work as an all-source intelligence analyst, sharing responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, your typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of a Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, help clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, coordinate data requests to substantiate or verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation, and support research for use in responding to collateral requests. Collaborate on complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, i.e., internal and external automated database systems, intelligence reports and case files. Contribute to detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups. Share recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and help establish new collection techniques for unique investigations. Support validation of sources and evaluate information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and assist in preparing production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts. Access local and national intelligence information databases to help respond to and validate requests for information. Help develop and maintain computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Coordinate liaison functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the intelligence communities.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, your typical work assignments may include:
Help clarify the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provide investigative leads, coordinate data requests to substantiate and verify information, suggest possible new avenues of investigation, and support research for use in responding to collateral requests. Collaborate on complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources. Contribute to detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups. Coordinate liaison functions with counterparts and personnel throughout the law enforcement communities. Support validation of sources and evaluate information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and assist in preparing production reviews from asset/informant cooperating witness validation efforts. Help develop and maintain computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports. Share recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and help establish new collection techniques for unique investigations.

Minimum Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. See www.sss.gov
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 grade level, performing the following duties:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Presenting briefings on a variety of intelligence topics to other law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions and recommendations; and
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience you may qualify for the GS-11 with a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a field of study related to this position such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, and sociology or other field of study that provides them with knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related
OR
Combination of education and experience. This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for GS-12, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level, performing the following duties:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Facilitates the investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Serves as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Utilizes seasoned judgement and experience in intelligence operations; and
Conducts long-range planning in assigned area of responsibility considering actual and potential problems and presents findings to supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for this grade level GS-12.

Eligibility under ICTAP: displaced Federal competitive service employees who are well-qualified (score 85 or better on established ranking criteria) may receive selection priority. Proof of eligibility must be provided with your application.
Eligibility under CTAP: surplus or displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice who are well-qualified (score 85 or better on established ranking criteria) may receive selection priority. A copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility must be provided with your application.
Veteran Preference: if entitled to veteran preference, indicate the type on your résumé and submit a copy of Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, official statement of service, or other official documentation showing military service was performed under honorable conditions. Disabled veterans, Purple Heart recipients, and qualifying family members must also submit the October 2013 Revised SF-15 and required supporting documentation.

cond_0250.intro:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Firearms Trafficking Intelligence Unit in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. The role functions as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0250.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-11, typical work assignments may include:
Under the guidance of a Senior Intelligence Research Specialist or Special Agent, clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate or verify information, suggests possible new avenues of investigation, and researches information for use in responding to collateral requests.
Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources, including internal and external automated database systems, intelligence reports, and case files.
Produces detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups.
Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations.
Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews of asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts.
Accesses local and national intelligence information databases to respond to and validate requests for information.
Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports.
Performs liaison and coordination functions with counterparts and personnel across the intelligence community as required.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-12, typical work assignments may include:
Clarifies the nature of investigative intelligence indicators, provides investigative leads, requests data to substantiate and verify information, suggests possible new avenues of investigation, and researches information for use in responding to collateral requests.
Performs complex analyses of raw primary and secondary data queried from various sources.
Produces detailed analytical reports on the activities of crime groups.
Performs liaison and coordination with counterparts and personnel across the intelligence and law enforcement communities as required by operational needs.
Conducts validation of sources and evaluates information derived from cooperating witnesses, assets, and informants, and prepares production reviews from asset/informant/cooperating witness validation efforts.
Develops and maintains computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports.
Makes recommendations for modifications and improvements to existing systems and establishes new collection techniques for unique investigations.
cond_0250.requirements:
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements:
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Pass drug screening and subject to random drug test.
Must successfully complete a background security investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
To qualify for GS-11, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 grade level in federal, state, or local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Collecting, analyzing, and disseminating intelligence information; using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Extracting, compiling, and analyzing factual information based on requests from special agents; and
Preparing and delivering briefings on intelligence topics to law enforcement and intelligence agencies and organizations; and
Maintaining and modifying computerized intelligence databases to generate statistical and relational reports; and
Drafting multiple, complex intelligence reports that contain original analyses, conclusions, and recommendations; and
Producing finished intelligence reports based on a review of data from various sources.
OR
In lieu of specialized experience, a Ph.D. Or equivalent doctoral degree, or three full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a degree in a related field such as social sciences, criminal justice, business and public administration, behavioral sciences, sociology, or another field that provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the position.
OR
LL.M., if related.
OR
Combination of education and experience, calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application.
To qualify for GS-12, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in federal, state, or local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Using a variety of intelligence-gathering methods including link analyses, visual investigative analyses, crime mapping, and telephone toll record analyses to support investigative operations; and
Facilitating investigations conducted by [Company name masked] and task forces; and
Serving as a technical consultant to management officials on intelligence issues affecting the division and [Company name masked]; and
Applying seasoned judgment and experience in intelligence operations; and
Conducting long-range planning in an assigned area of responsibility, considering actual and potential problems, and documenting findings for review by a supervisor or senior intelligence research specialist.
Substitution of education in lieu of specialized experience may not be used for GS-12.
